question: Which element’s symbol is derived from the Greek name hydrargyrum, meaning ‘liquid silver’ – indicating its shiny surface?
solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Mercury.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mercury's image** of Hg comes from its Greek call, hydrargyrum, meaning** "liquid silver", **because of its mobility and vibrant floor.
 
• Mercury is used in electrical switches of thermostats, but it is most commonly seen in the new compact fluorescent light bulbs.
 
• A heavy, silvery-white metal. The only metal (mercury) is liquid at room temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Antimony is a semi-metallic chemical element with an atomic** number 51** and the symbol Sb in the Periodic Table.
 
• **Zirconium (Zr),** a chemical element, the metal of Group 4 (IVb) of the periodic table, is used as a structural material for nuclear reactors.
 
• The symbol Ag derives from the Latin Argentum and Sanskrit argues from "bright". Silver was known in prehistoric times.
 
• It is used for jewelry and silver tableware.
